title: Sultanate of Palembang
capsule: The Palembang Sultanate emerged in the mid-15th century on the Musi River in southeastern Sumatra, succeeding the earlier Srivijayan and Majapahit-affiliated polities of the region. Its formal founding is attributed to Susuhunan Abdurrahman, who proclaimed the sultanate in 1659 after breaking from Mataram influence; Palembang became an important exporter of tin, pepper, and forest products. Dutch VOC pressure intensified through the 18th century, and following the Napoleonic-era interlude the returning Dutch deposed Sultan Mahmud Badaruddin II in 1821, abolishing the sultanate outright on 7 October 1823.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The sultanate's urban core and river-basin hinterland are documented in VOC records; the outer limits of tributary control over interior Sumatra are uncertain.
